newsitem.title: UK: Golf-Price seeks Dunhill Cup revenge.
newsitem.headline: Golf-Price seeks Dunhill Cup revenge.

text.p: Nick Price wants to recover from a string of setbacks by helping Zimbabwe to a first victory in the Alfred Dunhill Cup this week.

Price and team mates Mark McNulty and Tony Johnstone may receive an early chance to avenge defeat by Scotland in last year's final if they emerge in the same section in Wednesday's round-robin group draw.
Price's troubles this year include a debilitating sinus problem while leukaemia struck his close friend and caddy Jeff "Squeeky" Medlen.
Medlen's treatment continues but Price's problem has cleared up without the surgery he feared would be necessary.
A month ago his wife Sue gave birth to their third child, a girl named Kimberley Rae.

"My year's the wrong way round now. I'm getting keen and excited and I'm healthy again and it's the end of the year. But I've got six tournaments left so maybe I can still do some damage," said Price.
"May to August I played just five events. That's not enough. But I'm fine now and I've been practising a lot at home," added the former world number one whose ranking has plunged to 13th this year.
The 1994 British Open champion believes his team can win this 16-team medal match play event.
"Last year we played awfully well, all three of us, but it was tough to meet Scotland in the final."
"What you need in this event is for all three of you to be playing well. That's what Scotland did last year."
This year's event has drawn an imposing list of the world's great players, including three of the top four, world number one Greg Norman, number two Colin Montgomerie and number four Ernie Els.
Norman, playing for the 10th time and part of Australia's winning teams in 1985 and 1986, leads Steve Elkington and Wayne Riley -- a late replacement for Craig Parry -- into battle.
Montgomerie, fresh from clinching a fourth successive European Order of Merit title, links with Andrew Coltart, also part of last year's winning team, and promising newcomer Raymond Russell.
Els, Retief Goosen and Wayne Westner play for South Africa, Westner replacing David Frost. Like Parry, Frost has opted to try to qualify for the U.S. Tour Championship.
The Americans are favourites with a side comprising Phil Mickelson, Mark O'Meara and Steve Stricker.
They rank first, fourth and fifth on the U.S. Tour money list with a total of eight wins, four by Mickelson.
If Zimbabwe and Scotland do clash in the group phase, Johnstone will hope to face Coltart again.
Coltart holed in one against him in last year's final and holed a full seven-iron playing with him in Germany last week.
"If we play again, I'm going to show him how to hole a three-wood," Johnstone said.
